chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Where bebop's rhythms came from
summary: Patting rhythms on the leg, Klook's drumming and Feather's coinage of 'bebop'.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Right. Now, do you think that a lot of that kind of thinking and feeling, besides giving it the harmonic differences, but that that was at the core maybe of Bebop --

Well, he took that feeling and made a beautiful sentence out of it, you know. And it was just a pat-your-lap kind of thing. You know, guys would go just... [MAKES SOUND]... I don't know whether that picks this up. Yeah, all kind of ways, you know. And if a guy could do something... We used to...what did they call it...? This goes way back. I can't even think of the word they used to use for it. But it goes... I mean, where they used to hit their legs and they'd put notes to the rhythmic patterns that you had.

So that's how I think that Bebop started out, because most of the things were head rhythmic things, but it's just that they put notes to it and they'd start playing it, and they'd always coming out right. Like Dizzy wrote out "Salt Peanuts", you know...[SINGS 8 BARS]... Man, they were playing things like that on our legs, without the instrument. So I mean, you can see where it fits in.
Well, it's been said that some of those early riffs were drum-type riffs, and Kenny Clarke was involved with "Salt Peanuts" and things like that.
Yeah. Well, Klook used to make it, like BRRP-BOP, BRRP-BOP, in there... You could say "Be-Bop, Be-Bop, Be-Bop." But that's where Leonard Feather got the idea

of calling it "Bebop," because he would drop those bombs, and, you know, BRRP-BOP... And Leonard said, "Well, what could I call that. Bebop, okay." So he started to use the term "bebop." But Klook had been playing that for years.

But again, it's like you can play a phrase, and it might have the very same notes, you know melodically, and then by putting it in a different rhythmic pattern or putting it against at a different place in the structure tune...
You know, then it gives it a completely different feeling.
Yeah, it sure does. You can't go wrong with that.
